Several debates and forums took place among candidates in the campaign for the Democratic Party's nomination for president in the 2024 United States presidential election, which were sponsored by private organizations, rather than the party.

The Democratic National Committee expressed full support for incumbent president Joe Biden with no primary debates.[1] Although initially adamant that he would remain in the race, Biden ultimately withdrew on July 21 and endorsed Vice President Kamala Harris, who became the party's nominee on August 5.
Harris selected Tim Walz, the governor of Minnesota, as her running mate.

Reactions to the debate were mixed. _Politico_ described it as a dud,[25] while many attendees surveyed by _USA Today_ said they liked what they heard.[26] Both newspapers agreed that the debate would likely be inconsequential to the primary.
